title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
applicability: Binding in the EU on providers placing AI systems on the EU market and on deployers in the EU, and on non-EU providers or deployers where AI output is used in the EU. Echelon and Unbound have no EU market or EU output use established; rating: not applicable now, conditional if EU users appear. Staged dates per EUR-Lex: entry into force 2024-08-01; Chapters I and II (definitions, AI literacy, prohibitions) 2025-02-02; GPAI, governance and penalties 2025-08-02; general application 2026-08-02; new prohibitions added by the omnibus (Art. 5(1)(ba), (bb), 5(1a), 5(1b)) 2026-12-02; Article 50(2) for synthetic-content systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02 by 2026-12-02; Annex III high-risk obligations 2027-12-02; Annex I (product safety) high-risk 2028-08-02. Annex III includes creditworthiness of natural persons; DAF grant administration is not an Annex III category on its face.

title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
applicability: Amending act; see SRC-EU-AI-ACT for effect. Same applicability (not applicable now to Echelon).

title: Colorado SB 24-205, Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence (as amended by SB 25B-004; substantive provisions repealed and reenacted by SB 26-189)
applicability: The 'high-risk AI system' regime of SB 24-205 never took effect in its original form; SB 26-189 (signed 2026-05-14) replaced it with an automated decision-making technology (ADMT) regime. See SRC-COLORADO-SB26-189 for current applicability.

title: Colorado SB 26-189, Automated Decision-Making Technology
applicability: Binding in Colorado on developers and deployers of covered ADMT used to materially influence consequential decisions about individuals, including decisions on 'financial or lending services'. Developer documentation duties begin 2027-01-01; attorney general enforcement under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act with a 60-day cure period before 2030-01-01; no new private right of action. Unbound would be a developer only if it supplies ADMT that sponsors use to make consequential decisions about Colorado individuals. Typical DAF workflows (grant eligibility of charities, compliance screening) concern organizations, not consumers' access to financial services, but donor account approval or fraud holds could be argued as such. Rating: conditional, low likelihood; confidence low. Exemptions for entities complying with other legal obligations exist but were not read.

title: SR 11-7 / OCC Bulletin 2011-12, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
applicability: Superseded by SR 26-2 (2026-04-17). Questionnaires from bank-affiliated customers may still cite SR 11-7. Never bound Echelon.

title: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (interagency: Federal Reserve, OCC, FDIC)
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
applicability: Supervisory guidance for banking organizations (most relevant to those over USD 30 billion in assets). Supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8, emphasizing a risk-based, tailored approach. Does not bind Echelon. Reaches Unbound indirectly if a bank-affiliated customer treats an Unbound scoring, screening or AI component as a model (or vendor model) in its inventory and requests documentation, validation support and change notification. DAF sponsors themselves are charities, not banks. Rating: indirect, customer convention; confidence medium.

title: US state AI laws affecting automated decisions (umbrella)
applicability: Binding per state. Verified members so far: Colorado SB 26-189 and California CPPA ADMT regulations (effective 2026-01-01). Federal Executive Order 14365 (2025-12-11) addresses a national AI policy framework and state AI laws (content not read). Other state laws (for example on AI in employment or chatbot disclosure) are not verified here and mostly do not target DAF administration. Rating: conditional, low likelihood for current Unbound scope; confidence low.

title: Executive Order 14365, Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
applicability: Directs federal executive action; does not itself bind private companies or preempt state law. Relevant as a signal that state AI laws (including Colorado) may face federal challenge. Not applicable to Echelon directly.

title: NAIC Model Bulletin: Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems by Insurers
applicability: Applies to insurers through state adoption. Not applicable to Unbound (no insurer customers). Included for completeness.

title: PCI SSC Information Supplement: Penetration Testing Guidance v1.1
applicability: Explains tester qualification and organizational independence; useful beyond PCI as a widely cited definition of independence.

title: UK NCSC CHECK penetration testing scheme
applicability: Scheme for NCSC-assured companies testing UK public sector and CNI systems. Not applicable to Unbound unless it serves UK public sector or CNI.

title: Bank of England CBEST threat intelligence-led assessments implementation guide
applicability: UK regulator-led red teaming for systemically important firms and FMIs. Not applicable to Unbound as a US DAF platform.

title: TIBER-EU framework and DORA threat-led penetration testing (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Articles 26 and 27; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190)
applicability: Binding for EU financial entities identified by competent authorities; can reach ICT third-party providers in scope of a TLPT. Not applicable to Unbound unless it serves EU financial entities.

title: Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds banking organizations supervised by the Fed, FDIC and OCC, not Echelon. It reaches Unbound only when a bank or a bank-affiliated entity under bank supervision (for example a bank trust department or bank holding company affiliate acting as or supporting a DAF sponsor, or an ODFI reviewing the sponsor's payment vendors) contracts with or relies on Echelon. Then it flows down as due diligence questionnaires, contract terms (audit rights, incident notice, subcontractor oversight, business continuity, termination assistance) and ongoing monitoring. Most DAF sponsors are 501(c)(3) public charities that are not banking organizations, so for national charities and community foundations it is at most a reference point for what diligent sponsors may ask.

title: OCC Bulletin 2023-17, Third-Party Relationships: Interagency Guidance on Risk Management
issuer: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. OCC transmittal of the interagency guidance for national banks and federal savings associations. Reaches Echelon only if an OCC-supervised bank (or a sponsor whose bank affiliate applies OCC-driven vendor management) engages Unbound. Not applicable to stand-alone charitable sponsors.

title: FDIC FIL-29-2023, Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. FDIC transmittal to state nonmember banks. Relevant when a community foundation or other sponsor's bank, or a bank-affiliated sponsor, is FDIC supervised and treats Unbound as a third party. Community banks are a plausible ODFI for community foundation sponsors.

title: SR 23-4: Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Federal Reserve transmittal to all supervised banking organizations. Same reach as SRC-INTERAGENCY-TPRM-2023.

title: Third-Party Risk Management: A Guide for Community Banks
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Practical resource that community banks use to build vendor questionnaires. Matters to Echelon mainly as a predictor of what a community bank (for example the ODFI or depository bank of a community foundation sponsor) will ask of a payments-adjacent software vendor. Not binding on anyone.

title: FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook (IT Handbook InfoBase)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Examiner guidance for financial institutions and for examinations of technology service providers. Reaches Echelon if a bank or credit union customer relies on Unbound, or if Echelon were examined as a technology service provider under the Bank Service Company Act. Also the de facto vocabulary of bank vendor questionnaires, so useful as a design reference even where not applicable.

title: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook: Information Security booklet
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Most-cited booklet in bank vendor security reviews. Applies to Echelon only through a bank or credit union customer's vendor program or a service provider examination. Useful as a control checklist reference for Unbound regardless.

title: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook: Business Continuity Management booklet
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Drives resilience, recovery objective and third-party continuity questions from bank and credit union customers. Applies only through such customers.

title: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook: Development, Acquisition, and Maintenance booklet
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Covers SDLC, project management and supply chain risk; examiner expectations explicitly extend to entities including service providers. Relevant to Echelon's secure development evidence if a bank or credit union customer, or a service provider examination, is in scope.

title: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook: Architecture, Infrastructure, and Operations booklet
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Cloud, infrastructure and operations expectations; applies only through bank or credit union customers or a service provider examination.

title: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook: Outsourcing Technology Services booklet
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. The FFIEC booklet most directly about how institutions oversee technology service providers like Echelon. Applies only through bank or credit union customers or a service provider examination.

title: Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds banks and credit unions as supervisory expectation for customer and employee authentication, including access by third parties. Relevant to Unbound if a bank-supervised customer or ODFI evaluates Unbound's authentication for sponsor staff and donors. Good design reference for MFA and risk-based authentication even where not applicable.

title: Bank Service Company Act (12 U.S.C. 1861-1867)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Section 1867(c) subjects services performed for an insured depository institution by contract to regulation and examination by the institution's federal banking agency as if performed by the institution itself. If Echelon provides Unbound services to a bank (for example a bank trust department administering DAFs, or a bank that is itself the sponsor's agent), Echelon could be examined and the institution must notify its regulator of the service relationship. Does not reach services to stand-alone charitable sponsors.

title: Computer-Security Incident Notification Requirements for Banking Organizations and Their Bank Service Providers
issuer: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. A 'bank service provider' (one performing covered services under the Bank Service Company Act) must notify each affected banking organization customer as soon as possible when it determines it has experienced an incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, covered services for four or more hours (12 CFR 53.4 and counterparts). Binds Echelon directly only if Echelon serves a banking organization under the BSCA. For charity sponsors it is a useful benchmark for contractual incident notice terms.

title: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, Title V (privacy and safeguarding of nonpublic personal information), 15 U.S.C. 6801 et seq.
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Binds 'financial institutions' as defined (entities significantly engaged in financial activities). Whether a 501(c)(3) DAF sponsor is a GLBA financial institution is unresolved for this register; FTC Act jurisdiction generally excludes nonprofits, which weakens direct FTC enforcement against charity sponsors. Financial-institution-affiliated sponsors and their affiliates typically apply GLBA-grade controls by policy. Echelon receiving nonpublic personal information from a covered financial institution would be subject to reuse and redisclosure limits and to contractual safeguards. Whether Echelon itself is a financial institution because of DAF administration activities is an open question for counsel.

title: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards (12 CFR part 30 app. B; 12 CFR part 208 app. D-2; 12 CFR part 364 app. B)
issuer: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Requires banks to oversee service providers through due diligence, contractual safeguards and monitoring, and includes response program guidance (Supplement A) covering service provider incident notice. Reaches Echelon only through a bank customer. Not applicable to stand-alone charitable sponsors.

title: Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (16 CFR part 314)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds non-bank financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction. Section 314.4(f) requires them to select capable service providers, require safeguards by contract and periodically assess providers. Most DAF sponsors are nonprofits generally outside FTC Act jurisdiction, so direct application to sponsors is doubtful. If Echelon itself were found to be a non-bank financial institution, the rule would bind Echelon directly; that is an open legal question. Regardless, it is a widely used benchmark (qualified individual, risk assessment, MFA, encryption, annual board report, 30-day FTC notice for 500+ consumer events).

title: Regulation S-P: Privacy of Consumer Financial Information and Safeguarding Customer Information (2024 amendments)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds broker-dealers, registered investment advisers, investment companies and transfer agents. Flows down to service providers: covered institutions' policies must be reasonably designed to ensure service providers protect customer information and notify the covered institution as soon as possible, but no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a breach of a customer information system the provider maintains. Reaches Echelon only if Unbound processes customer information of a covered institution, for example where a financial-institution-affiliated sponsor's broker-dealer or adviser affiliate shares donor brokerage data with Unbound. The DAF sponsor charity itself is not a covered institution.

title: Identity Theft Red Flags Rules (Regulation S-ID, 17 CFR part 248 subpart C)
issuer: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; Commodity Futures Trading Commission
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds SEC-regulated entities that offer covered accounts. Requires oversight of service providers performing activities in connection with covered accounts. Reaches Unbound only if it performs such activities for a broker-dealer or adviser affiliate of a sponsor. Donor accounts at the charity sponsor are not securities covered accounts.

title: Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds SEC-reporting public companies (Form 8-K Item 1.05, Regulation S-K Item 106, which covers processes for overseeing risks from third-party service providers). DAF sponsors are not registrants; a public parent of a financial-institution-affiliated sponsor might pull Unbound into third-party risk processes only if the sponsor is within its cybersecurity risk management scope. Low likelihood.

title: Investment Advisers Act Rule 206(4)-7, Compliance procedures and practices (17 CFR 275.206(4)-7)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds SEC-registered investment advisers, whose compliance programs commonly extend to critical service providers. Reaches Unbound only if a sponsor-affiliated adviser (for example one managing DAF investment pools or a donor's recommended 'personal investment advisor' arrangement) relies on Unbound for an advisory function. Most Unbound functions are sponsor (charity) functions, not adviser functions.

title: Investment Advisers Act Rule 204-2, Books and records to be maintained by investment advisers (17 CFR 275.204-2)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds registered advisers. If an adviser keeps required records on Unbound, record retention, accessibility and electronic storage conditions flow down by contract. Not applicable to sponsor-only records.

title: Exchange Act Rule 17a-4, Records to be preserved by certain exchange members, brokers and dealers (17 CFR 240.17a-4), including electronic recordkeeping requirements
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds broker-dealers. Electronic recordkeeping conditions (audit-trail or WORM alternative, third-party undertaking) flow down only if a broker-dealer affiliate of a sponsor keeps required records on Unbound. Unlikely for core DAF administration.

title: FINRA Rule 3110, Supervision
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. SRO rule binding FINRA member broker-dealers; outsourcing does not relieve supervisory responsibility. Reaches Unbound only if a broker-dealer affiliate of a financial-institution-affiliated sponsor uses Unbound for a function it must supervise. The DAF sponsor charity is not a FINRA member.

title: FINRA Regulatory Notice 21-29, FINRA Reminds Firms of their Supervisory Obligations Related to Outsourcing to Third-Party Vendors
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Vendor due diligence and supervision expectations for member firms. Same reach as SRC-FINRA-RULE-3110: only through a broker-dealer customer or affiliate.

title: FINRA Rule 4370, Business Continuity Plans and Emergency Contact Information
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Member firms' BCPs must address critical business constituents. Only through a broker-dealer customer or affiliate.

title: FINRA cybersecurity guidance and Annual Regulatory Oversight Report (2026 edition)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. The 2026 report includes a section on the third-party risk landscape (marked new for 2026) and GenAI trends. Informs what broker-dealer affiliates of sponsors may ask about vendor and AI risk. Not binding on Echelon.

title: Cybersecurity Requirements for Financial Services Companies (23 NYCRR Part 500), as amended by the Second Amendment
issuer: New York State Department of Financial Services
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds DFS-licensed or chartered covered entities (state banks, trust companies, insurers, money transmitters and others). Section 500.11 requires a third-party service provider security policy (due diligence, MFA, encryption, incident notice). A charity DAF sponsor is not a covered entity; it reaches Unbound only if a sponsor is affiliated with a DFS covered entity that brings Unbound into its program, or if Echelon served a New York chartered trust company. Commonly used as a benchmark in vendor questionnaires.

title: Bank Secrecy Act and FinCEN regulations (31 U.S.C. 5311 et seq.; 31 CFR chapter X)
issuer: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, U.S. Department of the Treasury
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds BSA 'financial institutions' (banks, broker-dealers, money services businesses and others). A 501(c)(3) DAF sponsor is generally not a BSA financial institution, and Echelon is not one as a software provider unless Unbound were to transmit funds itself (it does not under CNV-PAY-001, where the sponsor originates through its bank). Reaches Unbound indirectly: sponsors' banks and brokerage custodians apply BSA controls to the sponsor, and sponsors may ask Unbound for KYC, beneficial ownership and suspicious activity escalation support. Money transmitter status should be re-examined if payment flows change.

title: Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Financial Institutions (CDD Rule)
issuer: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, U.S. Department of the Treasury
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds covered financial institutions in onboarding legal entity customers. A DAF sponsor is itself a legal entity customer of its bank; Unbound does not perform CDD under BSA. If sponsors choose to verify donors or grantees, that is policy, not CDD Rule compliance. Not applicable to Echelon directly.

title: OFAC sanctions regulations (31 CFR chapter V) and the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List
issuer: Office of Foreign Assets Control, U.S. Department of the Treasury
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly. OFAC prohibitions apply to all U.S. persons, including Echelon and every sponsor, on a strict liability basis. Echelon must not itself deal with blocked persons and must not facilitate prohibited transactions. Grant-recipient and donor screening is primarily the sponsor's compliance obligation, but because Unbound prepares and routes grant payments, sanctions screening support and evidence of screening will be a core diligence topic for all sponsor types.

title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
issuer: Office of Foreign Assets Control, U.S. Department of the Treasury
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Describes five components of a sanctions compliance program (management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, training). Sponsors use it to design their programs and will expect Unbound features and Echelon practices to support it. Echelon should also apply it proportionately to its own conduct.

title: U.S. Department of the Treasury Anti-Terrorist Financing Guidelines: Voluntary Best Practices for U.S.-Based Charities
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Voluntary guidance addressed to charities, including grantmakers; DAF sponsors use it to shape grantee due diligence, particularly for foreign grants. Flows to Unbound as product expectations (grantee vetting workflow, documentation). Not binding on anyone.

title: Internal Revenue Code section 4966, Taxes on taxable distributions (from donor advised funds)
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Imposes excise taxes on sponsoring organizations (and agreeing fund managers) for taxable distributions from DAFs, and defines 'donor advised fund' and 'sponsoring organization'. Binds the sponsor; flows to Unbound as core product requirements (grant eligibility checks, expenditure responsibility support for non-charity grantees, prevention of distributions to natural persons). Echelon is not a taxpayer under it, but defects in Unbound's grant controls translate directly into sponsor tax exposure and contractual liability.

title: Internal Revenue Code section 4967, Taxes on prohibited benefits
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Taxes donors, advisors and fund managers when a DAF distribution confers more than incidental benefit on a donor or advisor. Binds donors and sponsor managers; flows to Unbound as grant-recommendation attestations, benefit screening and documentation features.

title: Internal Revenue Code section 4958, Taxes on excess benefit transactions (including DAF provisions)
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Treats grants, loans, compensation and similar payments from a DAF to donors, advisors and related persons as automatic excess benefit transactions, and makes certain investment advisors disqualified persons with respect to sponsoring organizations. Binds sponsors' disqualified persons and managers; flows to Unbound as payee screening against donor and advisor relationships. Open question: whether Echelon or its personnel could ever be disqualified persons (for example if an Echelon principal is also a DAF donor or advisor on a sponsor using Unbound).

title: Internal Revenue Code section 170, Charitable contributions and gifts (deduction and substantiation)
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Governs donor deductions. Section 170(f)(18) conditions deductions for DAF contributions on a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the sponsor stating it has exclusive legal control; 170(f)(8) and related rules govern substantiation. Binds donors and shapes sponsor acknowledgment obligations; flows to Unbound's receipt and acknowledgment generation. Material 2025 change: Pub. L. 119-21 added a 0.5 percent floor and a non-itemizer cash deduction (170(p), up to $1,000 or $2,000 joint) that excludes contributions to establish or maintain a DAF. Unbound donor communications must not imply DAF gifts qualify for the non-itemizer deduction.

title: Pension Protection Act of 2006 (Pub. L. 109-280), title XII subtitle B part II donor advised fund provisions
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Source law for IRC 4966, 4967, the DAF changes to 4958, 170(f)(18) and Form 990 DAF reporting. Binds sponsors, donors and managers through those codified sections; see those records for flow-down.

title: IRS Publication 1771, Charitable Contributions: Substantiation and Disclosure Requirements
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Explains written acknowledgment and quid pro quo disclosure rules for charities. Sponsors must issue compliant acknowledgments; Unbound's receipt generation must support them. Not binding on Echelon; IRS publications are not authority, but reflect the binding code and regulations.

title: IRS Form 990 and Instructions for Schedule D (Form 990), Supplemental Financial Statements
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Schedule D Part I requires sponsoring organizations to report DAF counts, contributions, grants and values. Binds sponsors (filing obligation); flows to Unbound as reporting requirements. Form instructions are authorized by regulation but are not themselves regulations; authority type reflects the filing obligation.

title: Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Where enacted, governs management, investment and spending of institutional funds held by charitable institutions. Applies to sponsors (especially community foundations with endowed and DAF assets), not to Echelon. Whether particular DAF assets are 'institutional funds' depends on state enactment and fund terms; low direct effect on Unbound beyond investment and spending-policy reporting features.

title: Uniform Commercial Code Article 4A, Funds Transfers
issuer: Uniform Law Commission; American Law Institute
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Governs wholesale funds transfers, including non-consumer ACH credit entries, between the sponsor (originator), its bank and the beneficiary's bank. Allocates loss for unauthorized payment orders based on agreed commercially reasonable security procedures. Binds the sponsor and banks; flows to Unbound because Unbound's authentication, dual control and payment-file integrity are part of the sponsor's security procedure in practice, and sponsors will push liability for fraudulent payment instructions to Echelon by contract.

title: Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 section 404, Management assessment of internal controls (15 U.S.C. 7262)
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Binds SEC-reporting issuers and their auditors. DAF sponsors are charities, not issuers. Reaches Echelon only if a public company (for example the public parent of a financial-institution-affiliated sponsor) treats Unbound as relevant to its ICFR, which would show up as a SOC 1 Type 2 request. Low likelihood; more commonly SOC 1 demand comes from sponsors' own financial statement auditors.

title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Binds EU financial entities and, through them, ICT third-party service providers (Article 30 contract terms; critical ICT TPP oversight). Echelon serves U.S. DAF sponsors only and has no EU financial entity customers. Becomes relevant only if Unbound were offered to an EU financial entity or an EU-regulated affiliate of a sponsor relied on it.

title: EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02)
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Applies to EU credit institutions, investment firms, payment and e-money institutions. No EU customers; not applicable.

title: State unclaimed property laws (umbrella)
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Uncashed grant checks and unreturned funds can become reportable unclaimed property of the holder, normally the sponsor. Binds sponsors as holders; flows to Unbound as tracking of outstanding payments, dormancy dates, due diligence letters and reporting exports. Also binds Echelon directly for its own corporate property (for example uncashed vendor or payroll checks), which is outside this register.

title: State charitable solicitation and charity registration laws (umbrella)
issuer: U.S. states (attorneys general and secretaries of state, various)
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon's customer; flows down by contract or supervisory expectation. Binds sponsors that solicit contributions, and in some states may reach service providers that solicit or handle donations (professional fundraiser, fundraising counsel, commercial co-venturer or charitable fundraising platform categories). Echelon is a technology provider to sponsors, not a solicitor, but if Unbound hosts donor-facing solicitation for sponsors, state platform or fundraiser registration should be assessed. Open legal question.

title: Joint Statement on Community Banks' Engagement with Core Service Providers (SR 26-7)
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Addresses agency supervision of core technology service providers to community banks. Unbound is not a core banking provider. Relevant only as evidence of agencies' current posture toward service provider supervision under the BSCA.

title: AML/CFT Program and SAR Filing Requirements for Registered Investment Advisers and Exempt Reporting Advisers (FinCEN IA AML Rule)
issuer: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, U.S. Department of the Treasury
applicability: Rating: applies only if a particular customer type is served. Would bind SEC-registered and exempt reporting advisers from January 1, 2028. Relevant only where a sponsor's adviser affiliate relies on Unbound data for AML monitoring. Low relevance.

title: Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk by Regulators (OCC and FDIC final rule)
issuer: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Binds the agencies, not banks or vendors. Matters to this register because it amended Supplement A of the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards (12 CFR 30 app. B; 12 CFR 364 app. B) and coincides with removal of reputation risk language from FFIEC materials. Bank vendor questionnaires may drop reputation-based due diligence items.

title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 specifying the policy on contractual arrangements for ICT services supporting critical or important functions (DORA RTS)
applicability: Rating: not applicable. The RTS on ICT third-party policy referenced in the seed title for SRC-EU-DORA. Binds EU financial entities. Not applicable without EU financial entity customers.

title: EBA Guidelines on the sound management of third-party risk related to non-ICT services
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Will replace EBA/GL/2019/02 for non-ICT services. No EU customers; not applicable.

title: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act: ICT Accessibility Standards and Guidelines (36 CFR part 1194)
applicability: Binds federal agencies procuring ICT, not private vendors directly. Not applicable to Unbound's market, though the VPAT 508 edition derives from it.

title: Americans with Disabilities Act, Titles II and III, and DOJ Title II web and mobile accessibility rule (28 CFR part 35, subpart H)
issuer: US Congress; US Department of Justice
applicability: Title II binds state and local governments (WCAG 2.1 AA); compliance now due 2027-04-26 for entities of 50,000 or more population and 2028-04-26 for smaller entities and special districts. Not applicable to Unbound unless a public entity (for example a state university foundation that is a public entity) is a customer, in which case it flows down by contract. Title III (public accommodations) has no codified web standard; courts are split on whether websites of businesses without physical places are covered; DAF sponsors' donor portals face litigation risk, which they will push to vendors contractually. Rating: Title III indirect contractual, medium likelihood; Title II unlikely.

title: Directive (EU) 2019/882 on the accessibility requirements for products and services (European Accessibility Act)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
applicability: Binding through member state transposition for listed consumer products and services (including consumer banking services and e-commerce). Not applicable to Unbound absent EU consumer-facing services.

title: Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards (2 CFR part 200), procurement standards 200.317 to 200.327
applicability: Binds non-federal entities spending federal awards when they procure. A DAF sponsor would be bound only when buying with federal grant funds, which is atypical. Rating: unlikely.

title: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), including security and supply-chain clauses, under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul
issuer: FAR Council (GSA, DoD, NASA) and OFPP
applicability: Binds federal contractors through contract clauses. Not applicable to Unbound's market. Clause numbering is changing under the overhaul; do not rely on legacy clause citations without checking.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
applicability: Binding law, but applies to Echelon only if Unbound processes personal data of people in the EU in the context of offering services to them or monitoring them (Art. 3(2)), or if a customer subject to GDPR engages Unbound as processor. DAF donors are predominantly US taxpayers; EU-resident donors to US DAFs are possible but not established. Rating: unlikely, conditional. Customers still ask GDPR-style questions by convention.

title: UK GDPR (retained Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Data Protection Act 2018 and Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
applicability: Binding in the UK; reaches Echelon only on the same targeting or monitoring basis as EU GDPR. Rating: unlikely. DUAA 2025 changes (for example recognized legitimate interests, automated decision-making reforms) commence in stages; commencement status not verified.

title: EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (with UK Extension and Swiss-U.S. DPF)
issuer: European Commission (adequacy decision); US Department of Commerce (program)
applicability: Voluntary self-certification for US organizations under FTC or DOT jurisdiction. Only useful if Unbound receives EU, UK or Swiss personal data. Rating: unlikely; not recommended until an EU data flow is established.

title: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 on the concepts of controller and processor in the GDPR
applicability: Interpretive guidance; useful by analogy for drawing the controller (sponsor) versus processor (Unbound) line even under US law and contracts. Binding only as supervisory interpretation within the EU.

title: California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.) and CPPA regulations (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, div. 6)
issuer: California Legislature; California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA); California Attorney General
applicability: Binding on 'businesses' (for-profit entities meeting thresholds). Most DAF sponsors are nonprofit public charities and are generally outside the 'business' definition, and Echelon is unlikely to meet the thresholds (revenue, 100,000 consumers, or majority revenue from selling or sharing). Unbound would be a 'service provider' only for customers that are CCPA businesses. Commercial affiliates of sponsors may be businesses, but GLBA-covered data is exempted at the data level. Rating: conditional, low-to-medium likelihood; confidence medium.

title: CPPA regulations on CCPA updates, cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) and insurance
applicability: Binding on CCPA businesses. Adds risk assessments, annual cybersecurity audits and ADMT access and opt-out rights for covered businesses, with staged deadlines (not captured). Reaches Unbound only via CCPA-covered customers or if Echelon itself becomes a covered business; customers covered by it may push cybersecurity-audit evidence requests to service providers. Rating: conditional, low likelihood.

title: US state comprehensive consumer privacy laws (umbrella)
issuer: Various state legislatures; tracked by IAPP Westin Research Center
applicability: Binding in each enacting state on entities meeting that state's thresholds. Key nuance for Unbound: several state laws (for example Colorado, Oregon, Delaware, Minnesota and New Jersey, to be confirmed statute by statute) do not exempt nonprofits, so DAF sponsors and their processors may be covered where the CCPA would not cover them; most include GLBA exemptions that may be entity-level or data-level. Rating: conditional, medium likelihood for sponsors with large donor bases; confidence low until statute review.

title: US state data breach notification laws (umbrella)
applicability: Binding. All US states have breach notification statutes (per NCSL, not re-verified this pass); most require a third party that maintains data on behalf of another entity to notify the data owner promptly. Applies to Unbound as a maintainer of donor personal information for sponsors. Rating: likely applicable; confidence high in principle, details per state.

title: Regulation P, Privacy of Consumer Financial Information (12 CFR part 1016)
applicability: Binds financial institutions under CFPB jurisdiction regarding privacy notices and sharing of nonpublic personal information (NPI). DAF sponsors are generally 501(c)(3) charities, and whether a sponsor is a GLBA 'financial institution' is not established. The affiliated bank or broker-dealer is covered; if it shares NPI with Unbound (for example account linkage), the reuse and redisclosure limits (12 CFR 1016.11) and service-provider exception (1016.13) would flow to Unbound by contract. Rating: indirect or contractual; confidence medium-low.

title: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (S.C. 2000, c. 5)
issuer: Parliament of Canada; Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
applicability: Applies to organizations collecting personal information in commercial activity in Canada. Relevant only if Unbound serves Canadian donors or sponsors (Canadian DAFs are a separate legal regime). Rating: unlikely.

title: NYDFS Industry Letter: Guidance on Managing Risks Related to Third-Party Service Providers
issuer: New York State Department of Financial Services
applicability: Applies to 23 NYCRR Part 500 covered entities, which pass expectations to vendors. Recommends contract terms including MFA, encryption, prompt notice, data location limits, right to reject subcontractors, exit obligations and, for AI, whether the entity's data may be used to train AI models; ongoing monitoring with SOC 2 or ISO 27001 and pen test summaries; offboarding with certified deletion including backups. Relevant if any Unbound customer or its parent is DFS-regulated.

title: SEC Fact Sheet: Regulation S-P Amendments (Release 34-100155)
applicability: Covered institutions (broker-dealers, registered advisers, funds, transfer agents) must have written policies requiring oversight, including due diligence and monitoring, of service providers, and must ensure service providers notify them of breaches. Customer notice is due not later than 30 days. Drives RIA and broker-dealer questions to vendors such as Unbound when those firms share customer information with it.

title: Maryland DoIT System and Services Acquisition Standard MD-STD-317-SA-01
applicability: Binding on Maryland executive agencies; shows public buyer acceptance rules. Service providers must provide FedRAMP or GovRAMP authorization, a SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 from an accredited body, or another approved framework; a SOC 2 Type 2 counts only with an unqualified opinion showing operating effectiveness for CC6, CC7 and CC3.

title: OMB M-22-18, Enhancing the Security of the Software Supply Chain through Secure Software Development Practices (and companion M-23-16)
applicability: Rescinded by OMB M-26-05 on 2026-01-23. Historical only; customers may still cite it. Never bound Echelon directly (it bound federal agencies).

title: OMB M-26-05, Adopting a Risk-based Approach to Software and Hardware Security
applicability: Binds federal agencies only. Rescinds M-22-18 and M-23-16; agencies choose risk-based assurance and may require an SBOM on request (for cloud, an SBOM of the runtime production environment). Not applicable to Echelon unless selling to federal agencies; signals that SBOM-on-request is the federal norm that private buyers may copy.

title: BOD 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
applicability: Bound federal civilian executive branch agencies only. Revoked and superseded by BOD 26-04 (2026-06-10). Never bound Echelon; customer questionnaires may still cite its two-week and six-month timelines.

title: BOD 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk
applicability: Binds federal civilian executive branch agencies only; CISA states it does not bind private industry. Carries forward KEV criteria and harmonizes KEV with other patch timelines. Not applicable to Echelon; informative for remediation SLA design.

title: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Program (32 CFR part 170) and DFARS implementing rule
applicability: Binding only on defense contractors handling FCI or CUI under contracts with CMMC clauses. Not applicable to Echelon or Unbound absent DoD work.

title: CISA Binding Operational Directive 20-01: Develop and Publish a Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Binds federal civilian executive branch agencies only. Useful only as a model VDP structure for Echelon.

title: Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments
issuer: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly. OFAC sanctions regulations apply to all U.S. persons, including Echelon; the advisory explains how OFAC treats ransomware payments and the mitigating effect of prompt reporting and cooperation. Echelon's incident response plan should route any extortion demand through sanctions screening and law enforcement contact.

title: OMB Memorandum M-21-31, Improving the Federal Government's Investigative and Remediation Capabilities Related to Cybersecurity Incidents
issuer: Executive Office of the President, Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Bound federal agencies only, and it has been rescinded. Customers or questionnaires that still cite M-21-31 event logging tiers (EL0 to EL3) are using a withdrawn baseline; point them to M-26-14 if a federal logging reference is needed.

title: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022 (CIRCIA) and CISA implementing rulemaking
issuer: United States Congress; Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Reporting duties will fall on 'covered entities' in critical infrastructure sectors once a final rule takes effect. Some financial-institution-affiliated sponsors may become covered entities and flow 72-hour incident and 24-hour ransom payment notification needs down to Unbound by contract. Echelon itself is unlikely to be a covered entity; this depends on the final rule's definitions.

title: Interagency Guidance on Response Programs for Unauthorized Access to Customer Information and Customer Notice (Supplement A to Appendix B, Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards)
issuer: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; Office of Thrift Supervision (at issuance)
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Binds banks and their regulated affiliates. If a bank or bank trust affiliate is a sponsor, it must require its service providers to notify it of security incidents affecting customer information; this flows down to Unbound as contractual incident notice, cooperation and data-inventory duties. Not binding on non-bank sponsors.

title: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (CNSA 2.0) Cybersecurity Advisory and FAQ
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Binds vendors of products for U.S. National Security Systems. Relevant to Echelon only as a timeline signal for post-quantum migration.

title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability; Accessibility of Web Information and Services of State and Local Government Entities (ADA Title II, 28 CFR Part 35 Subpart H), as amended by the 2026 compliance date extension
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Binds state and local government entities (including public universities and their foundations if they are public entities), requiring WCAG 2.1 AA for web content and mobile apps, including content provided through contractors. Flows to Unbound only if a public entity sponsor or partner uses it. Most DAF sponsors are private nonprofits covered, if at all, by Title III, not this rule.

title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule (16 CFR Part 312), as amended 2025
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly only if triggered. Applies to operators of online services directed to children under 13 or with actual knowledge of collecting their data. Unbound is not child-directed; risk arises only if a sponsor enables youth or family giving accounts with child users. Then COPPA and the 2025 amendments (separate consent for third-party disclosure, written security program, retention limits) would apply. Nonprofits are generally outside FTC jurisdiction, but Echelon as a for-profit operator is not.

title: 11 U.S.C. 365(n): Rights of intellectual property licensees when a debtor-licensor rejects a license in bankruptcy
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly. If Echelon entered bankruptcy, sponsors licensing Unbound could elect to retain their license rights under 365(n). This underpins software escrow and continuity terms that sponsors request. SaaS access and hosted data may not be fully protected, which is why escrow and transition clauses matter.

title: Preventing Access to U.S. Sensitive Personal Data and Government-Related Data by Countries of Concern or Covered Persons (28 CFR Part 202)
issuer: U.S. Department of Justice, National Security Division
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly. Applies to all U.S. persons. Unbound holds personal financial data and identifiers of donors; if it exceeds bulk thresholds (for example personal financial data on more than 10,000 U.S. persons or covered personal identifiers on more than 100,000 in 12 months) it must not give countries of concern or covered persons access through data brokerage, vendor, employment or investment arrangements, including offshore contractors or subprocessors. Restricted transactions require a data compliance program and audits from October 6, 2025.

title: Colorado Privacy Act (SB21-190, C.R.S. 6-1-1301 et seq.) and rules (4 CCR 904-3)
issuer: Colorado General Assembly; Colorado Attorney General
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Colorado's act is one of the state laws that does not exempt nonprofits (not confirmed from the bill page), so a sponsor meeting its thresholds is a controller and Unbound a processor that must sign a processor contract and assist with consumer requests. Echelon may also be a controller for its own marketing data if thresholds are met (unlikely at current size).

title: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (SB 619, ORS 646A.570 to 646A.589)
issuer: Oregon Legislative Assembly; Oregon Department of Justice
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Applies to nonprofits from July 1, 2025, so DAF sponsors processing data of 100,000 or more Oregon consumers (or 25,000 with over 25 percent of revenue from selling data) are controllers and Unbound a processor. Expect processor contract terms and support for opt-out preference signals (required from January 1, 2026).

title: Internal Revenue Code section 6001, Notice or regulations requiring records, statements, and special returns
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly and flows down from customers. Requires every taxpayer, including Echelon and each sponsor, to keep records the IRS requires. For sponsors this drives record retention for contributions, grants and DAF activity that Unbound holds; Unbound retention and export must support it.

title: Internal Revenue Code section 6104, Publicity of information required from certain exempt organizations and certain trusts
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Sponsors must make their exempt applications and annual returns publicly available, while donor names and addresses on Schedule B are generally protected from public disclosure. Unbound reporting and exports must keep public-inspection copies separate from confidential donor data.

title: General Instructions for Certain Information Returns (Forms 1097, 1098, 1099, 3921, 3922, 5498 and W-2G)
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers and binds Echelon directly for its own vendors. Sponsors file 1099s for certain payments (for example to individuals or non-exempt payees); Echelon files for its own contractors. Unbound must capture TINs, support backup withholding status and produce IRIS-compatible data if sponsors use it for vendor or fee payments. Grants to 501(c)(3) charities are generally not 1099-reportable.

title: IRS Form 8283 (Noncash Charitable Contributions) and Form 8282 (Donee Information Return), with instructions
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Sponsors accepting noncash gifts (securities, real estate, crypto, closely held stock) sign donors' Form 8283 Section B and must file Form 8282 if they dispose of certain appraised property within three years. Unbound must track noncash gift intake, appraisal data, acknowledgment and disposition dates.

title: Treasury Regulations 26 CFR 1.170A-13 (Recordkeeping and return requirements for charitable contributions), with 1.170A-16 (substantiation for noncash contributions) and 1.170A-17 (qualified appraisal and qualified appraiser)
issuer: U.S. Department of the Treasury; Internal Revenue Service
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Defines the donor substantiation, contemporaneous written acknowledgment, appraisal summary and qualified appraisal rules that sponsors support for donors. Unbound gift acknowledgments and noncash gift workflows must produce compliant data.

title: IRS Publication 561, Determining the Value of Donated Property
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Explains fair market value and appraisal concepts for noncash gifts that sponsors and donors rely on; informs Unbound valuation fields and donor-facing guidance text.

title: IRS Digital assets guidance page
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Sponsors accepting crypto gifts must treat them as property (noncash gifts needing qualified appraisals above thresholds) and may receive broker reporting (Form 1099-DA). Unbound needs fields for asset type, units, appraisal and liquidation proceeds.

title: IRS Notice 2017-73, Request for Comments on Application of Excise Taxes With Respect to Donor Advised Funds in Certain Situations
issuer: Internal Revenue Service; U.S. Department of the Treasury
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Describes positions sponsors commonly follow: DAF grants should not pay for event tickets giving donors more than incidental benefit, should not fulfill a donor's personal pledge (with an approach Treasury was considering), and public support issues. Drives Unbound grant attestations and pledge-related controls.

title: Internal Revenue Code section 4943, Taxes on excess business holdings (including application to donor advised funds, 4943(e))
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Treats DAFs as private foundations for excess business holdings. Sponsors accepting closely held business interests must track combined holdings of the DAF and disqualified persons and divest within allowed periods. Unbound needs holdings, ownership percentage and disqualified-person relationship data.

title: Internal Revenue Code section 6115, Disclosure related to quid pro quo contributions
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Charities receiving a quid pro quo contribution over $75 must give a written statement estimating the value of goods or services. DAF grants should not involve quid pro quo benefits; Unbound should block or flag such grants and support sponsor direct-gift acknowledgments.

title: Treasury Regulations 26 CFR 53.4945-5, Grants to organizations (expenditure responsibility and good faith determinations, including equivalency determinations for foreign grantees)
issuer: U.S. Department of the Treasury; Internal Revenue Service
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Section 4966 borrows these rules: a DAF grant to a non-charity (including most foreign organizations) requires expenditure responsibility unless the sponsor makes a good faith (equivalency) determination, which may rely on current written advice from a qualified tax practitioner. Unbound must support equivalency determination records, ER pre-grant inquiry, agreements and reports.

title: IRS Form 4720 (Return of Certain Excise Taxes Under Chapters 41 and 42) and Instructions
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Sponsors and fund managers report and pay 4966, 4967, 4943 and 4958 excise taxes on this form. Unbound data must let a sponsor identify and document taxable distributions, prohibited benefits and corrections.

title: IRS Form 990 Schedule I (Grants to Organizations, Governments and Individuals in the U.S.), Schedule F (Activities Outside the U.S.) and Schedule L (Transactions With Interested Persons), with instructions
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Sponsors report domestic grants over $5,000 (Schedule I), foreign grants and activities by region (Schedule F) and transactions with interested persons (Schedule L). Unbound must produce grant data by grantee, purpose, region and relationship flags.

title: IRS Form 990-T (Exempt Organization Business Income Tax Return) and Instructions
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Sponsors holding gifted assets that generate unrelated business taxable income (for example pass-through interests in operating businesses, debt-financed property) may owe UBIT. Unbound needs K-1 and UBTI tracking at the fund or asset level for complex-asset sponsors.

title: Investment Company Act of 1940 sections 3(c)(10) and 7(e) (charitable organization exclusion and donor disclosure for charitable pooled income and similar funds)
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Charitable organizations and their pooled funds are excluded from investment company registration, but each fund excluded under 3(c)(10)(B) must give donors written information on its material terms. Sponsors that pool DAF assets in charitable investment pools rely on this; Unbound program disclosures and donor document delivery should support it.

title: Investment Advisers Act Rule 206(4)-2, Custody of funds or securities of clients by investment advisers (17 CFR 275.206(4)-2)
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Binds SEC-registered investment advisers. Reaches Unbound only where a sponsor's affiliated adviser manages DAF assets or where an advisor-managed DAF program brings adviser custody questions into scope. Echelon does not hold client funds or securities and is not an adviser.

title: CAN-SPAM Act of 2003 (15 U.S.C. 7701 to 7713) and FTC CAN-SPAM Rule (16 CFR Part 316)
issuer: United States Congress; Federal Trade Commission
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly. Echelon's own commercial email must comply. Unbound emails sent on behalf of sponsors are mostly transactional or relationship messages (statements, grant confirmations), but promotional messages to donors bring opt-out and sender identification duties that Unbound must support.

title: Telephone Consumer Protection Act (47 U.S.C. 227) and FCC rules (47 CFR 64.1200)
issuer: United States Congress; Federal Communications Commission
applicability: Rating: binds Echelon directly if Unbound sends texts or automated calls. SMS one-time passcodes, fraud alerts and donor notifications need consent handling and revocation processing; tax-exempt nonprofits have some exemptions, but Echelon as the sender platform should not rely on them.

title: California Government Code section 12599.9 (AB 488, charitable fundraising platforms and platform charities) and implementing regulations (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, sec. 300 et seq.)
issuer: California Legislature; California Attorney General, Registry of Charities and Fundraisers
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Applies to charitable fundraising platforms and platform charities soliciting in California. A DAF sponsor that runs donor-facing giving pages for many charities could be a platform charity or platform; Unbound could be treated as a platform if it enables solicitation rather than only providing technology. Requires registration, charity good-standing checks, donor disclosures and timely distribution.

title: Hawaii Revised Statutes chapter 467B, Solicitation of Funds From the Public (including charitable fundraising platforms and platform charities)
issuer: Hawaii State Legislature; Hawaii Department of the Attorney General
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Hawaii now regulates charitable fundraising platforms and platform charities (registration, $250 fee, annual reports). The definition of platform excludes a vendor that solely provides technical or supportive services to a platform, which is the position Unbound should document; a sponsor running donor-facing solicitation pages may be a platform charity.

title: Regulation E, Electronic Fund Transfers (12 CFR Part 1005)
applicability: Rating: not applicable (in most flows). Protects consumers' accounts. Grants from a DAF sponsor to charities are business-to-business payments; donor contributions by ACH debit from a consumer account are governed by Nacha authorization rules and Reg E protections apply to the donor's bank. Becomes relevant if Unbound ever initiates consumer debits as more than a sponsor's TPSP.

title: Uniform Commercial Code Articles 3 (Negotiable Instruments) and 4 (Bank Deposits and Collections), with 2002 amendments
issuer: Uniform Law Commission; American Law Institute
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Governs checks: sponsors that still pay grants by check bear loss rules for forged or altered checks and the duty to review statements. Drives Unbound requirements for check issuance data, positive pay files and reconciliation.

title: Regulation CC, Availability of Funds and Collection of Checks (12 CFR Part 229)
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (funds availability)
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Binds banks; affects how quickly grantees can use funds from sponsor checks and remote deposits. Background for check-based grant payment design.

title: Regulation J (12 CFR Part 210) and Federal Reserve Banks Operating Circular No. 6, Funds Transfers Through the Fedwire Funds Service
issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Reserve Banks
applicability: Rating: not applicable. Binds Fedwire participants (banks). Relevant when sponsors pay large grants by wire; since July 14, 2025 Fedwire uses ISO 20022 messages, so wire instruction data in Unbound should be ISO 20022 compatible.

title: PCAOB AS 2201, An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Binds auditors of SEC issuers. Reaches Unbound only if a public-company sponsor affiliate treats Unbound as relevant to its ICFR and its auditor relies on a SOC 1 report. Most DAF sponsors are not SEC issuers.

title: FinCEN Alert on Nationwide Surge in Mail Theft-Related Check Fraud Schemes Targeting the U.S. Mail (FIN-2023-Alert003)
issuer: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), with the U.S. Postal Inspection Service
applicability: Rating: flows down from customers. Directed at financial institutions, but it is strong evidence for sponsors moving grant payments from paper checks to ACH and for using positive pay. Supports Unbound payment-method and check-control requirements.

title: Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.303, Internal controls (federal awards)
applicability: Rating: applies only for certain customer types. Binds recipients of federal awards. Most DAF sponsors do not receive federal awards; a community foundation managing federal grant funds would need internal control and cybersecurity safeguards (200.303(e)) and could flow those to Unbound.
